title: Finite and countable sets: counting, enumeration, and examples
summary: Count finite sets, enumerate integers and rationals, and prove that subsets, images, finite unions, and finite products of countable sets are countable.
abstract: Counting a finite set gives a number that does not depend on how its elements are arranged. For infinite sets, the corresponding question is whether every element can appear in a list whose positions are the natural numbers. The integers and rational numbers both admit such lists and are called countable. This ability to list elements survives taking subsets or outputs of functions, combining finitely many countable sets, and forming ordered lists of a fixed finite length from them.
